To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) Japanese English bilinguals exhibit semantic accents in L2 and L1, (b) culture specific features are more strongly associated with words of the congruent language, and (c) culture specific features become more strongly associated with L1 words and less strongly associated with L2 words after many years of L2 cultural immersion.

Japanese English bilinguals have a stronger association than English monolinguals and Japanese monolinguals have between culture specific features of one language and words in the language of the other culture.

1) bilinguals exhibit semantic accents in both L1 and L 2, 2) bilinguals have stronger feature based associations between culture specific semantic features and words in the congruent language, and 3) the strength of semantic accents in L2 is related to L2 cultural immersion rather than L2 proficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cultural immersion in bilinguals' semantic development and its impact on their L1 and L 2 processing.
the development of feature based models that can account for the processing of culture specific semantic features in bilinguals.
the role of culture specific features in semantic accents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processing of semantic accents is affected by L2 cultural immersion, but not L2 proficiency.
semantic accents in Japanese and English bilinguals are a result of cultural immersion and are influenced by the relative proficiency of each language.
semantic accents are influenced by the strength of associations between features and words in both languages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the processing of semantic features is influenced by both the L1 and L 2 cultures, and that the L2 culture has a stronger influence on L2 than the L1 culture has on L1.
the feature based model of bilingual semantic processing can be used to understand semantic accent phenomena.
culture specific features are important to bilingual language processing and are more strongly associated with words in the congruent language.
The main takeaway from our work is that
semantic accents are not simply a matter of L1 and L1 cultural immersion but also L2 cultural immersion.

semantic accents can be examined by a feature based approach, and that the strength of associations between culture-specific features and words in the incongruent culture is dependent on L2 cultural exposure.
feature based models are useful in capturing the effects of a semantic accent.
